questions.question: What is the correct way to declare a variable with the type string in TypeScript?
Which TypeScript feature allows defining custom types?
What does the TypeScript keyword 'readonly' do?
alternatives: Marks a property as immutable after initialisation
Makes a class method return only primitive types
Prevents a class from being extended
Restricts a variable to read operations only at runtime
questions.correctAnswer: Marks a property as immutable after initialisation

questions.question: Which of the following correctly defines a TypeScript enum?
alternatives: enum Direction { Up, Down, Left, Right }
enum Direction = { Up, Down, Left, Right }
const enum = Direction { Up, Down, Left, Right }
type Direction = enum { Up, Down, Left, Right }
questions.correctAnswer: enum Direction { Up, Down, Left, Right }

questions.question: What is a TypeScript 'type guard'?
alternatives: A runtime check that narrows a variable's type within a conditional block
A compile-time decorator that prevents type widening
A utility type that makes all properties optional
An interface that enforces strict null checks
questions.correctAnswer: A runtime check that narrows a variable's type within a conditional block
